correctness.rationale: Clauwens tensor cokernel has det(I−τ)=det(I−T)(1−det T). When detT≠1 the enveloping group is V⋊Z and its derived subgroup V is characteristic, proving similarity up to inverse. Rational canonical form yields (p−2)(p−1)+(p−3) quandle classes. Similarity to inverse would force detT=−1 and trT=0, contrary to connectedness. Direct matrix checker tests full F_p² matrices for p=3,5,7,11, cokernel dimensions and complete conjugacy orbits for p=3,5, and the p=5 inner-group collision. General proof is symbolic, not extrapolated from tests.

originality.rationale: The exact nonresonant prime-square comparison and p²−2p−1/2 count were not found in the inspected sources. Clauwens supplies a general group model; Nelson supplies quandle module classification; the new deduction combines a characteristic derived subgroup, rank-two conjugacy counting, the resonance determinant boundary, and a genuinely different inner-group identification. Search absence is not treated as proof, and alternative terminology is a priority risk.
residual_risks: An earlier explicit classification of rank-two metabelian semidirect groups under alternate group-theoretic language may give an equivalent prime-square count.
The result is a classification derived from known general group and quandle structures, not a claim that those structures themselves are new.
Tensor-category equivalence may occur without group isomorphism; none of those additional possibilities are classified.

value.rationale: The 2026 dual-quandle examples motivate asking exactly which nonisomorphic prime-square Alexander quandles have the same group-theoretic representation invariant. A complete rank-two classification, exact class count and determinant-one central-resonance boundary give a natural invariant census, and the explicit same-inner/different-enveloping pair demonstrates information loss between fundamental symmetry objects. Neither a renamed existing general group formula nor an arbitrary small numerical case.
